new.title: Walk through the Vogtsbauernhof open-air museum
new.desc: The Black Forest Open Air Museum in Gutach gathers original farmhouses, mills and workshops, centred on the Vogtsbauernhof of 1612. It shows how farmers, craftsmen and clockmakers lived in the Kinzig valley.
new.tip: Open daily from late March to early November, 9:00 to 18:00; the museum has its own S-Bahn stop on the Offenburg to Hornberg line. Check vogtsbauernhof.de for 2027 dates.

new.title: Climb the Feldberg tower, the Black Forest's roof
new.desc: At 1,493 metres the Feldberg is the highest mountain in the Black Forest. The Feldbergturm on its summit area gives views to the Alps in clear weather, and the Schwarzwälder Schinkenmuseum sits inside the tower.
new.tip: Reach it by the Feldbergbahn chairlift or on foot from the Feldberger Hof car park. Go on a clear morning for the Alpine view.

new.title: See the Master HL altarpiece in Breisach Minster
new.desc: St. Stephansmünster crowns the Münsterberg above the Rhine in Breisach. Inside are the late Gothic high altar carved by Master HL around 1526 and Martin Schongauer's Last Judgement fresco.
new.tip: The panorama from the minster terrace over the Rhine and Alsace is free. Entry to the church is free, with a small charge for the altar viewing in some seasons.
new.q: Breisacher Münster St. Stephan, Münsterplatz, Breisach am Rhein

new.title: Hike up to the Staufen castle ruin above the vines
new.desc: The ruined Burg Staufen stands on a hill above the town, set among Markgräflerland vineyards. The town is also tied to the legend of Dr. Faust, said to have died at the Löwen inn here in about 1540.
new.tip: The path from the market square takes about 20 minutes. Combine with a coffee in the old town afterwards.
new.q: Burgruine Staufen, Schlossbergweg, Staufen im Breisgau

new.title: Admire the Advent-calendar town hall of Gengenbach
new.desc: Gengenbach has a well-preserved half-timbered old town in the Kinzig valley with a baroque Rathaus. Each December its 24 windows turn into the largest Advent calendar in the world, opened one per evening.
new.tip: The calendar windows open at 18:00 daily from 1 December. The old town is free to wander and quiet on weekday mornings.

new.title: Explore the Hochburg ruin, a huge fortress near Emmendingen
new.desc: The Hochburg is the largest castle ruin in Baden, built from the 12th century and expanded as a Baden-Durlach fortress. It was blown up by French troops in 1689 and now stands as a wooded ruin above Emmendingen.
new.tip: Free to enter; there is a ruin restaurant and a wide Rhine plain view. The walk up from Emmendingen takes about an hour.

new.title: Climb Rötteln Castle above the Wiesental
new.desc: Burg Rötteln near Lörrach is one of the largest castle ruins in Baden-Württemberg, with a history going back to the 11th century. It was held by the Lords of Rötteln and later the Margraves of Baden-Hachberg before French forces destroyed it in 1678.
new.tip: From the keep tower there are views to the Rhine and the Vosges. The castle restaurant and an annual castle festival are held in summer.

new.title: Tour the Vitra Campus and Design Museum in Weil am Rhein
new.desc: The Vitra Design Museum by Frank Gehry opened in 1989 and is part of a campus with buildings by Zaha Hadid, Tadao Ando, Álvaro Siza and Herzog and de Meuron's VitraHaus. The campus is a pilgrimage for architecture fans on the German-Swiss border.
new.tip: The campus can be walked for free; the museum and architecture tours need tickets. Weil am Rhein is a short tram or train ride from Basel.
new.q: Vitra Design Museum, Charles-Eames-Straße 2, Weil am Rhein

new.title: Stand under the great dome of St. Blasien Cathedral
new.desc: The Domkloster St. Blasien has a rotunda dome of 36 metres in diameter, completed in 1783 after a fire and one of the largest church domes in Europe. The former Benedictine abbey houses a Jesuit college today.
new.tip: Free to enter. The nearby Rothaus and Schluchsee areas make an easy day loop.
new.q: Dom St. Blasien, Kurhausstraße, St. Blasien

new.title: Cross Europe's longest covered wooden bridge
new.desc: The Holzbrücke in Bad Säckingen spans the Rhine to the Swiss town of Stein and is about 200 metres long. A wooden bridge has stood here since the 13th century, and the current structure dates from 1700.
new.tip: Free and pedestrian only; walk across and back for about 15 minutes. The Fridolinsmünster and Trompeterschlösschen are close by.

new.title: Visit Ortenberg Castle above the Kinzig plain
new.desc: Schloss Ortenberg is a 19th century neo-Gothic reconstruction of an older castle above the Ortenau vineyards. It served for decades as a youth hostel and offers views across the Rhine plain.
new.tip: Check opening for the interior; the vineyard paths below are free. Pair it with the Sieferle Straußwirtschaft in Ortenberg in autumn.

new.title: Marvel at the Rococo library of St. Peter Abbey
new.desc: The former Benedictine Kloster St. Peter in the Black Forest village of the same name holds one of the finest Baroque church interiors in the region and a Rococo library from the 1700s. It was a Zähringer burial site from the 12th century.
new.tip: The abbey church is open daily; abbey tours run on set days, so check the village tourist office before travelling.
new.q: Kloster St. Peter, Klosterhof, St. Peter (Schwarzwald)

new.title: Stroll around the Mummelsee on the Schwarzwaldhochstraße
new.desc: The Mummelsee is a glacial cirque lake at about 1,030 metres below the Hornisgrinde. Black Forest legend says water spirits, the Mummeln, live in it.
new.tip: Free parking along the Hochstraße fills early at weekends. A paved loop of about 20 minutes circles the lake.

new.title: See the Todtnau Waterfall, 97 metres in cascades
new.desc: The Todtnau Waterfall drops about 97 metres in several tiers through a rocky gorge between Todtnauberg and Aftersteg. It is a protected natural monument and one of the highest waterfalls in Germany.
new.tip: A short path leads down from the Hangloch bus stop, and the Wasserfallsteig hiking trail passes it. After heavy rain or snowmelt the flow is greatest.

new.title: Discover Waldkirch's organ-building and barrel-organ history
new.desc: Waldkirch in the Elz valley was a centre of barrel-organ and fairground-organ building from the 19th century. The Elztalmuseum shows these instruments and the local history.
new.tip: Check opening days on the town website; the museum is quite compact. A barrel-organ festival is held in the old town in some years.

new.title: Walk Waldshut's old town between its two gate towers
new.desc: Waldshut is a Habsburg-founded town on the Rhine whose old town is built along the Kaiserstraße, closed by the Obertor and Untertor. The Rhine and the Swiss shore lie just below.
new.tip: The old town is compact and best seen in an hour. In August the Chilbi folk festival fills the streets.

new.title: Take a boat tour or row on Lake Titisee
new.desc: Titisee is a glacial lake at 840 metres and one of the most visited spots in the Black Forest. The operator Schweizer has run lake cruises since the early 1900s, with a roughly 25-minute commentary trip and rowing or pedal boats for hire.
new.tip: Visit early or off-season to avoid crowds. The 7 km lake loop trail makes a good walk.

new.title: Hike the Wutach Gorge, the Black Forest's Grand Canyon
new.desc: The Wutachschlucht is a deep river canyon with wild forest, limestone walls and waterfalls, and a protected nature reserve. It is considered one of the most rewarding hikes in southern Germany.
new.tip: The trail from Schattenmühle toward Räuberschlössle is rough and has sections with ropes. Wear sturdy shoes and avoid after heavy rain.

new.title: Paddle or sail on the Schluchsee reservoir
new.desc: The Schluchsee is the largest lake in the Black Forest, a reservoir created in 1932 for hydropower. It is a popular spot for sailing, pedal boats, swimming and the 18 km lake path.
new.tip: Rental boats are available on the north shore in summer. Water is cool even in July.
new.q: Bootsverleih Müller, An der Staumauer 1, Schluchsee-Seebrugg

new.title: Spend a day in Europa-Park Rust
new.desc: Europa-Park in Rust opened in 1975 and is the largest theme park in Germany. Its themed European quarters and roller coasters like Silver Star draw millions of visitors a year.
new.tip: Buy tickets online and arrive at opening. The park runs a winter season with an Alpine theme; check the official calendar.

new.title: Ride the Hasenhorn Coaster summer toboggan in Todtnau
new.desc: The Hasenhorn Coaster at Todtnau is a long summer toboggan run on a rail track, reached by chairlift. It has been listed among the longest such runs in Germany.
new.tip: Prices were listed at about 15 EUR for adults. It is closed in poor weather, so check hasenhorn-rodelbahn.de before travelling.

new.title: Cross the Blackforestline suspension bridge over the falls
new.desc: The Blackforestline is a 450-metre suspension bridge opened in May 2023 above the Todtnau waterfall gorge. Its ticket also grants entry to the waterfall.
new.tip: Bus line 140 stops at Hangloch, under 200 metres from the western bridgehead. Not for those afraid of heights.

new.title: Ride the steam Kandertalbahn from Kandern to Haltingen
new.desc: The Kandertalbahn, nicknamed Chanderli, is a heritage railway between Kandern and Haltingen operated by the Zweckverband Kandertalbahn and Kandertalbahn e.V. since 1986. Steam trains run along the valley on scheduled days.
new.tip: Check the current timetable on kandertalbahn.de; steam runs on set Sundays and holidays in season.

new.title: Ride up and hike on the Belchen, the southern Black Forest's lookout
new.desc: The Belchen rises to 1,414 metres above the Münster valley and gives a view over the Alps, the Vosges and the Rhine plain on clear days. A cable car climbs from Münstertal.
new.tip: Take the Belchenbahn up and walk the ridge trail. Check the lift's opening days before going.

new.title: Climb the Kandel above Waldkirch
new.desc: The Kandel is a 1,241-metre peak above the Elz valley, with a view from the Vosges to the Alps. It is also a well-known hang-glider and paraglider launch.
new.tip: Drive or take the Kandel bus part way and finish on foot. Paragliders launch from the summit area on good days.

new.title: Hike the moor plateau of the Hornisgrinde
new.desc: At 1,164 metres the Hornisgrinde is the highest peak in the northern Black Forest, with a moorland plateau and a tower. The Mummelsee lies on its western flank.
new.tip: Take the loop path from the Mummelsee, about two hours. Bring a jacket as it is windy and cool at the top.

new.title: Walk the Ravenna Gorge to the stone railway viaduct
new.desc: The Ravennaschlucht is a narrow gorge near Breitnau. It is crossed by the stone arches of the Ravenna viaduct of the Höllentalbahn, which can be reached from the Hofgut Sternen.
new.tip: Start at the Hofgut Sternen car park; the gorge route is short. In winter a Christmas market is held under the viaduct.

new.title: Soak in the thermal pools of Bad Krozingen
new.desc: Bad Krozingen is a spa town on the edge of the Black Forest with a thermal spring and the Vita Classica Therme. Spring water rich in carbon dioxide feeds its pools and park.
new.tip: Bring a swimsuit and allow half a day. Weekdays are quieter.
new.q: Vita Classica Therme, Herbert-Hellmann-Allee 12, Bad Krozingen

new.title: Watch ski jumpers fly off the Adler Schanze in Hinterzarten
new.desc: Hinterzarten is a centre of German ski jumping and Nordic combined, with a complex of jumps used for the summer Grand Prix. The village lies on the Höllental route near Titisee.
new.tip: Summer Grand Prix events are held in the warmer months, and winter competitions in snow; check the Hinterzarten events listing.

new.title: Ride the Feldbergbahn chairlift to the Seebuck
new.desc: The Feldbergbahn takes visitors from Feldberg-Bärental up the Seebuck, with a view of the Feldsee glacial lake and the summit. In winter the area is the largest ski region in the Black Forest.
new.tip: Combine it with the walk to the Feldbergturm. Ride tickets are bundled with the tower museum entry.

new.title: Watch glassblowers at the Hofgut Sternen
new.desc: The Hofgut Sternen in Breitnau has a glassblowing workshop where visitors watch vases, oil lamps and glass baubles made from glass tubes. The estate sits at the entrance of the Ravenna Gorge.
new.tip: Check opening times for the glassblowing demonstrations; they run mainly on weekdays.

new.title: Drink a Tannenzäpfle at the Rothaus brewery inn
new.desc: The Badische Staatsbrauerei Rothaus was founded in 1791 by the St. Blasien abbey and brews the cult Tannenzäpfle pils. The Brauereigasthof next door serves local dishes with the beer.
new.tip: The inn is open daily; the restaurant listing shows lunch and dinner hours. Brewery visits and the Erlebnispfad need advance booking.

new.title: Taste the story of Black Forest ham at the Schinkenmuseum
new.desc: The Schwarzwälder Schinkenmuseum in the Feldbergturm explains how Black Forest ham is dry-cured and smoked over conifer wood. The ham has held EU protected geographical status since 1997.
new.tip: Open daily 9:00 to 17:00 with shorter off-season hours; entry is free with a Feldbergbahn ticket. Buy a smoked ham in the valley afterwards.

new.title: Eat a Vesper at the Löffler Strauße in Staufen
new.desc: Weingut Löffler runs a seasonal Strauße at its estate in Staufen-Wettelbrunn, serving its own Markgräfler wines with simple regional food. It sits among the vineyards below the Staufen castle hill.
new.tip: Open in season only, so check opening dates before going. Order a Gutedel with a Vesper board.
new.q: Löffler Strauße, Fohrenbergstraße 43, Staufen im Breisgau

new.title: Sit in the Vogelstrauße in Oberbergen for Federweißer
new.desc: The Vogel family farms about six hectares of wine and fruit in Vogtsburg-Oberbergen and runs a Straußwirtschaft in autumn. The menu includes Zwiebelkuchen, pumpkin and plum dishes and new sweet wine.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran 29 August to 1 November, with Tuesday and Wednesday closed. Try Zwiebelkuchen with Neuer Süßer.

new.title: Join locals at the Bürkle-Strauße in Mahlberg
new.desc: Weingut Bürkle in Mahlberg opens a seasonal Strauß in the Breisgau wine foothills, listed in the Badische Weinstraße Straußen guide.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran until 25 October. Open Thursday to Saturday from 17:00, Sundays and holidays from 16:00.

new.title: Taste Ortenau wine at the Sieferle Straußwirtschaft
new.desc: Familienweingut Sieferle in Ortenberg runs a seasonal Straußwirtschaft among the Ortenau vineyards, one of the longest-running Straußen in the area.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran until 28 November, Tuesday to Saturday from 17:00. Pair it with a walk up to Schloss Ortenberg.

new.title: Eat at s'Dolle Frieders Burewirtschaft in Sasbachwalden
new.desc: This Strauße in the wine village of Sasbachwalden is listed as one of the special Black Forest Straußwirtschaften. It opens only in two seasons a year.
new.tip: Open mid-May to the end of July and mid-August to mid-October. Order a regional Vesper with Ortenau wine.

new.title: Taste Kaiserstuhl Pinot at Weingut Dr. Heger in Ihringen
new.desc: Weingut Dr. Heger is a leading estate in Ihringen on the volcanic Kaiserstuhl, a warm wine-growing hill near the Rhine. Spätburgunder and Weißburgunder grow here on vineyards like the Winklerberg.
new.tip: The shop is open Monday to Friday 9:00 to 12:00 and 13:30 to 18:30 in season. Ask about a tasting.

new.title: Dine at the Schwarzer Adler of Franz Keller
new.desc: The Weingut Franz Keller in Oberbergen is a Kaiserstuhl wine estate whose restaurant Schwarzer Adler has held a Michelin star since 1969. The estate is known for its Spätburgunder from steep volcanic vineyards.
new.tip: Reserve ahead for dinner. For a cheaper visit, ask about the estate's KellerWirtschaft and wine tasting.

new.title: Visit the Bickensohler Weinvogtei winery
new.desc: The Bickensohler Weinvogtei is a winegrowers' cooperative in Vogtsburg-Bickensohl, a village on the southern Kaiserstuhl. It sells local Grau- and Spätburgunder from volcanic soil.
new.tip: Open weekdays 9:00 to 17:30 from April to October. Try a Grauburgunder.

new.title: Sip Kirschwasser at Schladerer in Staufen
new.desc: The Alte Schwarzwälder Hausbrennerei Schladerer began in 1844 when Sixtus Schladerer distilled Kirschwasser at the Kreuz-Post inn in Staufen. It is a well-known fruit-brandy house of the Black Forest.
new.tip: Distillery tours were listed on request from April to October (Wednesdays at 14:00); a visitor centre was planned, so confirm first.
new.q: Schladerer Hausbrennerei, Alfred-Schladerer-Platz 1, Staufen im Breisgau

new.title: Visit the Kaiserstühler Winzer Ihringen cooperative
new.desc: The Winzer Ihringen cooperative sells wines from Ihringen, Germany's warmest wine village. Cellar tours and tastings are offered.
new.tip: Ask about cellar tours and tastings; opening hours change by season.
new.q: Kaiserstühler Winzer Ihringen eG, Winzerstraße 6, Ihringen

new.title: Eat in the SchwarzwaldStube at Hofgut Sternen
new.desc: The Hofgut Sternen in Breitnau is a historic inn at the Ravenna Gorge, linked in tradition to Marie Antoinette and Goethe. Its SchwarzwaldStube restaurant serves German and Black Forest cooking.
new.tip: Open for lunch and dinner. Combine it with the Ravenna Gorge walk and glassblowing workshop.
